<!-- ABOUTME: Records why the SIGINT fixture tests wait for shell state instead of elapsed time. -->

# SIGINT fixture conditions on card #623

The SIGINT forcings waited for a one-second deadline at head because the shell intentionally remained in a FIFO read. That made the passing path depend on elapsed time. The caller now instruments its private command fixture with a marker immediately after bare `wait`. The `ps` route waits for that marker and, when the shell can exit, for its zombie state before cleanup sends the group kill. The Node route waits for the marker and, when the shell can exit, for Node's exit event before sending SIGINT. Neither passing path waits for a deadline.

This marker is written only into the fixture copy under the test's scratch directory. The shell's exit status and its FIFO read remain the same. In the pilot with the old `command` fixture, both tests failed with dispatch exit 0; with the FIFO fixture, both passed with dispatch exit 137. These pilots ran on an uncommitted tree and are not counted as A11/A12 head evidence. The counted runs belong to the committed and pushed head.

The earlier `c623-red-init.log` was a draft-test defect: `elsewhere()` invoked `git init -q` inside `withFirstOnPath`, so the hanging `git` stand-in was first on PATH and the draft test ended after 131,010 ms. The final test calls `elsewhere()` before `withFirstOnPath`.

Two A26 dispositions remain questions for the card author. `c623-affected.log` is an affected-file suite run from a fresh clone before `npm ci`; `test/worktrees.test.mjs` failed to import `acorn`. The PR's `check (24)` job in run 38515570251 failed `C615 Mac group full tool exit census` in an unchanged test with an empty recorded nonce. The run lasted 212.718791 ms at that test, so the host-stall exception is unsupported, and no open root-cause card names it. The maker cannot decide whether the pre-install run falls outside A26 or select a root-cause card for the CI failure.

The first revision commit hook refused the commit after a full suite with 12 failures. Its end load was 31.11, and a concurrent `uptime` reading while it ran was 107.55. An unrelated static architecture test took 101.411583 ms in that run versus 0.748958 ms in the earlier fresh-head suite, 135.4 times longer. The eleven `never-stop` failures have the host-stall and #697 dispositions. The `exit-cleanup` failure was caused by this card's `command` fixture: its `mkfifo` ran after readiness and introduced an extra group member for cleanup to kill. The earlier claim that the staged code had no effect on any failure was wrong. The complete original output is below, with trailing spaces rendered as `␠`; the FIFO-order repair is recorded in the later #623 journal entry.
